memories.memory: I usually vote for candidates who protect voting access, public schools, and Social Security, even when I disagree with their economic policies.
In 2022, I donated $600 from my savings to a regional voting-rights organization and volunteered twice at its community information table.
I consider myself spiritually curious but not religious; after attending a Unitarian discussion group in Cedar Falls for about a year, I decided organized religion was not for me.
I believe the criminal justice system should focus more on rehabilitation, which is why I have supported restorative-justice programs at the county level for several years.
My strongest political conviction is that older adults should be able to make their own medical and end-of-life decisions without family members or politicians overriding them.
I am more supportive of accepting refugees than most people in my extended family, and holiday dinners sometimes turn tense when immigration comes up.
Although I do not identify with any political party, I joined a local coalition in March 2024 that opposed selling the town's public housing land to a private developer.
